title: Social media needs a reset button

sentences: We yearn to remake ourselves each new year.
The calendar inspires us to drink less or exercise more, learn new things, spend more time with friends and family.
We also might want to start the year on a social media diet.
But for that particular New Year's resolution, the deck is stacked against us.
To change how we interface with Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, we need an easy-to-use reset button that offers a clean break from our online histories.
translations: 我们渴望在每个新年重塑自我。
日历激励我们少喝酒或多锻炼、学习新事物、花更多时间与朋友和家人相处。
我们也可能想在新年伊始进行社交媒体节食。
但对于那个特定的新年决心，形势对我们不利。
要改变我们与Instagram、TikTok和YouTube互动的方式，我们需要一个易于使用的重置按钮，它能让我们与在线历史彻底决裂。

sentences: Legislators are pushing for warning labels on social media, but mere warnings do not go far enough.
Instead, users should be given the tools to turn off their individualized algorithms and see random content.
With a single click, the social media companies could be prohibited from pushing you targeted feeds from companies and pundits.
You would have the option to start afresh, just as you do when deciding to join a gym or begin a new hobby to start the new year.
translations: 立法者正在推动在社交媒体上添加警告标签，但仅靠警告远远不够。
相反，用户应该获得关闭个性化算法并查看随机内容的工具。
只需点击一下，社交媒体公司就可能被禁止向你推送来自企业和专家的定向信息流。
你将有机会重新开始，就像你决定在新年加入健身房或开始一项新爱好时那样。

sentences: To understand what a reset button would do, consider how your social media feed works now.
Every time you pause on a post, click a link, or like a video, the platform's algorithms take note.

Over months and years, the service builds an increasingly detailed profile of your preferences — and particularly the topics that anger you, the creators who keep you scrolling, the products you might buy.
This profile then determines almost everything you see, generating a feed custom-designed to keep you engaged based on your past behavior.
translations: 要理解重置按钮的作用，先想想你现在的社交媒体信息流是如何运作的。
每当你在一篇帖子上停留、点击一个链接或点赞一个视频时，平台的算法都会记录下来。
经过数月乃至数年，该服务会构建出越来越详细的偏好档案——尤其是那些让你愤怒的话题、让你不停刷屏的创作者、以及你可能购买的产品。
这个档案随后决定了你几乎看到的一切，生成一个根据你过去行为量身定制的信息流，旨在让你保持参与。

sentences: A reset button would wipe this profile clean, leaving the algorithms with no history to work with.

Now your feed could show you random popular content, posts in simple chronological order, or a genuine mix of viewpoints rather than an endless loop of content similar to what kept you clicking yesterday.
translations: 一个重置按钮会清空这个个人资料，让算法没有历史记录可参考。
现在，你的信息流可以向你展示随机热门内容、按简单时间顺序排列的帖子，或者真正的观点混合，而不是像昨天让你不断点击的类似内容那样无休止地循环。

sentences: This sort of reset already exists in other contexts.
Universities offer fresh start policies to let students with rocky academic beginnings regroup away from school and then come back and recommit with a clean transcript.
Many states now prohibit students from accessing smartphones during the school day.
If restarts and breaks make sense in these contexts, why not offer consumers a simple self-help tool for something that the previous US surgeon general labeled a public health "emergency"?
translations: 这种重置在其他情境中已经存在。
大学提供重新开始的政策，让学业起步不顺的学生离开学校重新调整，然后带着干净的学业记录回来重新投入。
许多州现在禁止学生在校期间使用智能手机。
如果重新开始和休息在这些情境下有意义，那么为什么不为消费者提供一个简单的自助工具，来应对前美国卫生局局长所称的公共卫生“紧急情况”呢？

sentences: At this point, we all know that social media can be bad for us.
An army of Silicon Valley scientists constantly wage war on our attention, making it difficult for us to detach from screens.
The algorithms curating our content are optimized for personal outrage, polarizing us instead of bringing us together.
And even as social media tailors itself to our individual tastes, it breeds a culture of sameness.
Locked inside our own online echo chambers, we marinate in the same political opinions, the same music, the same cultural content, instead of being challenged.
translations: 在这一点上，我们都知道社交媒体可能对我们有害。
一群硅谷科学家不断对我们的注意力发动战争，使我们难以脱离屏幕。
策划我们内容的算法针对个人愤怒进行了优化，使我们两极分化，而不是让我们团结在一起。
即使社交媒体根据我们的个人品味量身定制，它也滋生了一种同质化的文化。
被困在我们自己的网络回音室里，我们沉浸在相同的政治观点、相同的音乐、相同的文化内容中，而不是受到挑战。

sentences: True, platforms currently offer some voluntary options for refreshing the algorithms that control your content.
And you can always delete your account entirely.
But the hard lesson of the past 15 years is that users need help.
Intentionally challenging interfaces make adjusting your settings easier said than done.
Even someone who takes the initiative to change their settings will still be targeted with ads based on their digital histories.
And deleting your account is not always a realistic option given social media's popularity and importance in some workplace contexts.
translations: 确实，平台目前提供了一些自愿选项来刷新控制你内容的算法。
而且你随时可以完全删除你的账户。
但过去15年的惨痛教训是，用户需要帮助。
故意设计得难以操作的界面使得调整设置说起来容易做起来难。
即使主动更改设置的人，仍会基于其数字历史记录被定向投放广告。
考虑到社交媒体在某些工作环境中的普及性和重要性，删除账户并不总是一个现实的选择。

sentences: From childproof drug containers to automobile backup cameras, we already mandate simple and safe measures for certain products.
To give social media users a fighting chance, legislators need to mandate a prominent one-click means for ditching our online histories.
translations: 从儿童安全药瓶到汽车倒车摄像头，我们已经对某些产品强制实施了简单且安全的措施。
为了让社交媒体用户有机会保护自己，立法者需要强制推行一种醒目的一键式方法来清除我们的在线历史记录。

sentences: Some might object that this proposal is paternalistic.
But the reset option could be calibrated to address different concerns.
First and foremost, resets need not last forever.
After all, tailored content is not all bad, and many of us would not want to permanently abandon any consideration of personal relevance in our feeds.
Consumers could be given the option to go back to their original profiles or choose whether or not they want to be tracked in the future.
Even during a voluntary reset, accommodations could be made for preserving existing connections to the accounts of family, friends, and support groups.
We don't need to let the perfect be the enemy of the good — the important thing is to give users a fighting chance at a real digital detox.
translations: 有些人可能会反对说，这个提议带有家长式作风。
但重置选项可以进行调整，以应对不同的担忧。
首先，重置不必永久持续。
毕竟，个性化内容并非一无是处，我们中的许多人也不愿永久放弃在信息流中考虑个人相关性。
消费者可以选择恢复原始个人资料，或决定未来是否愿意被追踪。
即使在自愿重置期间，也可以做出调整，以保留与家人、朋友和支持团体账户的现有联系。
我们不必让完美成为美好的敌人——重要的是给用户一个真正数字排毒的机会。
